title: Agitation
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute agitation, aggression, psychomotor activation, and possible threatening behavior. Priority: ensure safety of patient and staff. Determine etiology: psychiatric (schizophrenia, bipolar mania, psychosis) vs substance-induced (stimulants, PCP, alcohol withdrawal) vs medical (hypoglycemia, hypoxia, head injury, sepsis, encephalopathy). Rapid assessment: vital signs, fingerstick glucose, pulse oximetry, brief neuro exam. Verbal de-escalation first-line. If pharmacologic needed: PO preferred over IM if patient willing — lorazepam (benzo) or olanzapine (antipsychotic). If IM required: midazolam + haloperidol or olanzapine IM. Avoid physical restraints unless absolutely necessary — can worsen agitation and cause rhabdomyolysis. If restraints used: 1:1 observation, frequent monitoring. Once stabilized → workup for underlying cause (tox screen, CT head, labs). Psychiatry consult.
